where: The Old Light, floor 5 — The Gallery of Confident Facts (wrong captions, a waxed floor, banana skins)
mood: Confident Facts — a pompous brass fanfare that keeps landing on proudly wrong notes.
_note: Classic oldlight-f5: 112, F 'allegedly', wrong notes held loud and proud, whole-tone tumbles. Opening: a pompous fanfare that misfires onto a wrong chord and carries on regardless.
core_styles: 16-bit console RPG soundtrack from the mid-1990s
retro sampled-chip instruments with the warm echo of a 16-bit sound chip
F major with deliberately wrong notes
grand brass fanfare that keeps landing on proudly wrong notes and clashing chords
tuba and timpani marching with mock solemnity
comic pomposity, a museum gallery full of confident nonsense
strong singable melody, instantly hummable and pleasant on repeat

sections.name: Intro
sections.text: {a grand trumpet fanfare that misfires onto a wrong, clashing chord, a beat of shock, then it marches on proudly regardless}

sections.name: Main Theme
sections.text: {the march tune as a pompous processional on trumpets and trombones over tuba and timpani, with notes held loud and proud on the wrong pitch; the half cadence becomes a whole-tone xylophone tumble}

sections.name: Main Theme Reprise
sections.text: {again with French horns adding a counter-melody that lurches up a whole tone and back, the band insisting it is correct}

sections.name: Bridge
sections.text: {contrast: a pompous minor-key aside, D minor declared major halfway, harp whole-tone glissandi and a lecturing bassoon, then a fanfare run home that lands on the wrong chord and corrects itself}

sections.name: Main Theme Return
sections.text: {the pompous march returns; the last bar's run home lands slightly wrong and tumbles straight back into the theme}
styles: seamless loop back to the start of the theme
